defects.title: R517's LCSC pick is not the true highest-stock candidate the report claims, and the report's Q8/Q9 SQL still carries the exact TEXT-vs-numeric Stock sort bug the review-fix pass explicitly found and fixed for J500/JP500/JP510 in this same report
defects.evidence: Report §2 queries 8 and 9 use `ORDER BY "Library Type", Stock DESC` (Stock is SQLite TEXT, same bug as the original queries 4/5) and the report states for R517 'Top Extended... C23000 (0603WAF3012T5E), stock 74,544 - selected.' Running the query with a correct `ORDER BY CAST(Stock AS INTEGER) DESC` over the same WHERE clause (Package='0603' AND Description LIKE '% 30.1kΩ %') returns C137745 (RC0603FR-0730K1L) at stock 425,894 - genuinely the top row, ~5.7x more stock than C23000, same package/value/tolerance/tempco class ('100mW 30.1kΩ 75V Thick Film Resistor ±1% ±100ppm/℃'). The literal query as printed in the report, run with a LIMIT and no CAST, does not even surface C23000 as its nominal top row (a raw run of the printed Q8 query returns chaotic ordering topped by a 91-unit-stock part) - meaning the report's stated selection process does not actually produce the part it claims to have picked; the real justification (unstated) appears to be 'same Uniroyal 0603WAF family as the rest of the sheet', not the stock-ranking rationale the report writes down. R516 shows the same pattern on a smaller scale: report picks C23068 (51,539) over the true top C2930111 (FRC0603F5231TS, 54,790, ~6% more stock, same spec).
defects.fix: Either (a) correct R517's LCSC to the genuinely top-stock, footprint/spec-matching row (C137745, 425,894 in stock) and regenerate, updating C23000 -> C137745 in the generator, schematic and report (with a fresh netlist_diff proof), or (b) if the Uniroyal-family-consistency rationale is intentional, rewrite report §2 queries 8/9 to state that as the actual selection criterion instead of the currently-false 'Top Extended... selected' stock claim, and fix the SQL to use CAST(Stock AS INTEGER) so it doesn't silently misrepresent the ranking the way queries 4/5 originally did. R516 should get the same treatment (correct to C2930111 or document the real criterion) for consistency, though its stock gap is small enough to be a minor issue on its own.
